clue.text: Half-cut bandleader perhaps led capitally?

definitions.note: written in capitals, led becomes LED, a light-emitting diode, which is one kind of this device

parts.note: read as 'half', cut off as a prefix: semi- means half
a bandleader is one example of a conductor, who directs an orchestra or band

explanation.surface: A tipsy bandleader is said to have led his band splendidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' looks like slang for drunk, and 'capitally' like 'splendidly'; instead 'led' in capitals is LED, the light-emitting diode, an example of the answer, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An LED is a diode made from a material that conducts electricity only partly, so it is an example of this electronic component.

clue.text: Whack small child

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a mite is an affectionate word for a small child

explanation.surface: Someone is told to hit a little kid, a grim instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To whack someone is to strike them hard, and the verb in the answer means to hit with force.

clue.text: Arab leader offended by Spooner's crude arrangement

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two pieces trade places

parts.note: a sheikh is an Arab chief or ruler
miffed means put out or offended

explanation.surface: An Arab ruler is upset by a rough-and-ready set-up, as Spooner would say it.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'sheikh miffed' with its opening sounds swapped becomes 'make shift'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something makeshift is a temporary, rough substitute, a crude arrangement put together for the moment.

clue.text: So mum tells baby pretty little finger has one

indicators.note: the way a mother coos in baby talk to her infant, so the words are heard as she would say them

parts.note: pretty is cute, and 'ickle' is baby talk for little

explanation.surface: A mother tells her baby its tiny finger is so pretty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cute ickle', baby-talk for 'pretty little', run together sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Every fingernail has a thin strip of skin at its base, so each finger has one.

clue.text: Don't worry, it's not Gore's favoured campaign weapon

parts.note: no serves as a negative here, like not
a cause is a campaign or movement one supports
Al Gore is the former US vice-president; favoured means 'for', so 'for Al'
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: Reassurance that something is not a weapon Al Gore would use while campaigning.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Gore, US vice-president under Clinton, supplies AL after FOR (in favour of).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom reassuring someone that there is nothing to be anxious about.

clue.text: Not in nude, strangely not recognised

indicators.note: the first word goes inside the rearranged letters of the next
strangely says the letters of nude come out in an odd order

explanation.surface: Something odd about not being in the nude went unremarked.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Not in nude' as one phrase about clothing; 'strangely' makes UNED, split by the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not recognised has gone unremarked, and the answer means not observed or noticed.

clue.text: Leader of tribe's eldest perhaps possessive

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the eldest child is often the heir, the one who will inherit

explanation.surface: A tribal chief's eldest child may be possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: This word is a possessive pronoun, the form saying something belongs to them.

clue.text: Refill Pilsner? He's drunk!

indicators.note: a drunk man is all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the pronoun he; the 's is read as 'is', linking to the anagram signal

explanation.surface: A drinker asks for his lager to be topped up, being already drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To refill a glass is to fill it again, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: What not to do with scab (or so we're told)?

definitions.text: What not to do with scab (or so we're told)?

parts.words: What not to do with scab (or so we're told)?
parts.note: we are told not to pick a scab; 'pick it' heard aloud gives the word for striking workers who stand outside to turn away scabs, strikebreakers

explanation.surface: Parental advice not to pick at a healing wound.
explanation.walkthrough: A scab is also a strikebreaker, whom strikers confront at the gates; the advice 'don't pick it' sounds like the word for that.
explanation.definitionFit: Strikers stand at a workplace gate to dissuade strikebreakers, so this is what one does with a scab, punning on 'pick it'.

clue.text: Endlessly drained after continued lack of respect

indicators.note: after places the drained piece behind the abbreviation
endlessly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a drained glass is empty

explanation.surface: Someone drained after long effort shows a lack of respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt is scorn, a complete lack of respect for someone.

clue.text: Makes match midweek

definitions.meaning: to marry or join two people together
the abbreviation for Wednesday, the middle day of the week

explanation.surface: A sports fixture is made in the middle of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means marries, making a match; the abbreviation names Wednesday, the middle of the week.

clue.text: Instruction as to which seeds go in first?

definitions.meaning: a judge's ruling or direction issued by a law court

definitions.text: as to which seeds go in first?
definitions.meaning: in tennis, seeded players are ordered onto the courts, read as an order of play on court

explanation.surface: Gardening advice on which seeds to sow first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeds' suggests gardening, but they are tennis seeds, the ranked players.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's direction is an instruction from a legal court; jokingly it is also the order of play on tennis courts.

clue.text: Reported high point for ecstasy tablets — no more from China

indicators.note: reported means the words are heard as spoken rather than written

parts.note: a peak in Es: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, and a peak is a high point

explanation.surface: Rumours of a high from drug-taking, with no more supply from China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no more from China' means from Peking, a name no longer used for Beijing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means of Peking, the old name of China's capital, now called Beijing, so a place no more.

clue.text: Sent to Gate 4?

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet, as gates are often lettered

explanation.surface: Someone is directed to gate number four at an airport.
explanation.walkthrough: Gate 4 becomes entrance D, the letter in fourth place.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sent is to be carried away with delight, so in this sense sent means enchanted.

clue.text: Affliction took over flower

indicators.note: over means the pieces are turned over, read backwards

parts.note: an ail is an ailment or affliction
had means took, as in had a biscuit

explanation.surface: An illness took hold of a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a garden plant with showy flowers, named after the botanist Dahl.

clue.text: Election preceded and followed by different attempts to get attention of the masses

indicators.note: these words put one piece before the election and another after it

parts.note: hoi and oi are two different calls to get someone's attention
a poll is an election or vote
hoi and oi are two different calls to get someone's attention

explanation.surface: Politicians shout at an election to get the public's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is Greek for 'the many', used for ordinary people, the common masses.

clue.text: Old dictator staging comeback is having trouble with hearing device

indicators.note: a comeback goes back, so the dictator's name runs backwards

parts.note: Tito was the dictator of Yugoslavia

explanation.surface: An old tyrant returning to power is having problems with a hearing aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing device' is the ear, not a hearing aid.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is inflammation of the ear, trouble with the organ we hear with.

clue.text: Goon becomes wild

indicators.note: wild says the letters of becomes run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A fool turns wild.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goon Show was a 1950s BBC radio comedy; Harry Secombe was one of its stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Secombe was one of the Goons, the comic trio of the British radio show.

clue.text: Get the better of totally, force overcoming resistance

indicators.note: force overcoming resistance means F, for force, beats out R, for resistance, taking its place

parts.note: outright means totally, completely

explanation.surface: Total victory is won by force overcoming resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: In physics F stands for force and R for resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat an opponent in combat is to get the better of them.

clue.text: Beat endless deception of religious writings

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat them

indicators.note: endless says the last letter goes

parts.note: a trick is a deception

explanation.surface: Someone defeats a never-ending deceit in sacred texts.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the tantras, Hindu and Buddhist religious texts.

clue.text: Garland for Young Conservative with former labour minister on platform

indicators.note: on places the speakers on the platform, after it in this across answer

parts.note: a dais is a raised platform
YC is the abbreviation for a Young Conservative
Peter Hain was a minister in the Labour government

explanation.surface: A floral garland is given to a young Tory sharing a stage with an old Labour minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Hain was a cabinet minister under Blair and Brown.
explanation.definitionFit: A string of flowers linked stem to stem makes a garland.

clue.text: Holy man had us transported

indicators.note: transported means moved from place to place, shifting these letters

explanation.surface: A holy man carried us along.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu is a Hindu ascetic, a holy man.

clue.text: The man following company turnover must line up here to get on the board

definitions.text: line up here to get on the board

indicators.note: following puts the man after the company
turnover means the word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: he refers to the man

explanation.surface: A man trailing behind on a firm's staff turnover must join the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get on the board' sounds like company directors, but it is the dartboard.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the line darts players stand behind to throw at the dartboard.

clue.text: Where parasite's found on a plant

indicators.note: in this down answer, on puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: a parasite lives on its host

explanation.surface: A query about where a parasite lives on a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a leafy garden plant, also called a plantain lily.

clue.text: American accountant tried returning to scholarly life

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

indicators.note: returning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: aimed means tried, as in aimed to finish

explanation.surface: An American accountant tries going back to university life.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of universities, scholarship and study.

clue.text: Enjoy being kind of related?

parts.note: rel. is the abbreviation for related
the suffix -ish means kind of, somewhat

explanation.surface: A question about enjoying being sort of family.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish something is to enjoy it greatly.

clue.text: Democrat Brown's record almost complete after European body finds a contrived solution

indicators.note: after puts the record behind the European body

parts.note: EU is the European Union

indicators.note: almost complete means all but the final letter

parts.note: James Brown recorded the funk hit Sex Machine

explanation.surface: A Democratic politician called Brown almost finishes a record after the EU finds a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown is James Brown, the soul singer, not Gordon Brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'god from the machine', it is a plot device that resolves a story artificially.
